a: A clinic vaccinates 300 residents against flu in October
b: A clinic does nothing in October while flu circulates
note: Prevented harm counts as an outcome; doing nothing leaves the counterfactual harm in place.

a: An actor plays a surgeon in a hospital drama
b: A surgeon removes a patient's appendix in a hospital
note: Depiction versus the act: form acting versus surgery, content medicine in both.

a: Two friends watch a new documentary about bees
b: A critic writes a review of a new documentary about bees
note: A: form differs (spectating versus reviewing), content is the same documentary; B (production) differs too, since one consumes and the other produces.

a: A teacher explains photosynthesis to a class
b: A teacher explains the causes of the French Revolution to a class
note: Same act, different subject matter.

a: A man reads a recipe aloud to his daughter
b: A man cooks the recipe for his daughter
note: Reading about an act versus performing it; content (cooking) is the same.

a: A farmer opens an irrigation channel and the field greens within a week
b: A farmer opens an irrigation channel and the water drains away without reaching the field
note: Same act, observable change differs.

a: A man phones his sister from his kitchen
b: A man phones his sister from his office desk
note: Setting only (home versus work sphere); a vocabulary without setting should collide here by design.

a: A student revises for an exam in the city library
b: A student revises for an exam in her bedroom at home
note: Setting only (public institution versus home).

a: A girl plays chess with her grandfather
b: A girl plays football with her grandfather
note: Different kind of play; the shared partner and relation are not the form.

a: A mechanic replaces the worn brake pads on a car
b: A mechanic inspects a car's brake pads and finds them fine
note: A repair changes the car; an inspection with no finding changes nothing.

a: A council clears a blocked drain before the storm and the street stays dry
b: A council leaves a blocked drain alone and the street floods in the storm
note: Invisible prevention versus a realised harm.

a: A lifeguard dives in and brings a swimmer to the shore
b: A lifeguard sits on the chair while a swimmer goes under
note: Act versus omission; the outcome (rescue versus drowning risk) differs.

a: A man buys a book about gardening
b: A man buys a book about astronomy
note: Same purchase, different subject matter.

a: A man writes a letter to his landlord
b: A man reads a letter from his landlord
note: Producing versus receiving a text; content (the tenancy) is the same.

a: A surgeon cuts open a patient's abdomen with the patient's signed consent
b: A stranger cuts open a man's abdomen with a knife
note: Near-identical act and material; consent and informedness differ, which is layer B (informedness, volition, signed impact), so A-identical is expected.

a: A patient's headache clears after she takes a sugar pill she believes is aspirin
b: A patient's headache clears after she takes aspirin
note: Attribution against the predicted counterfactual: the drug should carry causal contribution, the placebo little.

a: Residents refuse to buy from a chain store to protest its labour practices, and its takings fall
b: Residents happen to shop elsewhere for a month because of a road closure, and the chain's takings fall
note: An omission credited relative to the counterfactual (boycott) versus a coincidence; volition and causal contribution differ.

a: A man wins a lottery draw and receives a large prize
b: A man wins a prize for a business plan he worked on for two years
note: Luck versus effort: attribution should route little of the lottery win to the man.

a: One council member's vote makes a 5 to 4 majority pass the budget
b: A council passes the same budget by 9 to 0
note: Degree of responsibility versus additive share; value routing stays additive.

a: A man donates money to a charity
b: A man hands money to a charity after being threatened
note: Volition as a record (a prior threat event); the act looks the same.

a: A pharmacist hands a customer the pills and explains the interaction warning
b: A pharmacist hands a customer the pills without mentioning the interaction warning
note: Informedness as a record (disclosure delivered).

a: An employee signs a supply contract on behalf of her company
b: An employee signs a supply contract for her own business
note: Acting for versus acting for oneself.

a: A diner hands ten euros to a waiter after the meal
b: A driver hands ten euros to a traffic officer who then waives a fine
note: Same transfer, count-as rule differs (tip versus bribe).

a: A driver hands ten euros to a traffic officer who then waives a fine
b: A shopper pays ten euros of sales tax at the till
note: Same sum to an agent of a body; counts as bribe versus tax.

a: A diner hands ten euros to a waiter after the meal
b: A shopper pays ten euros of sales tax at the till
note: Tip versus tax: voluntary gratuity versus levy.

a: A parent gives a child ten thousand euros for a birthday
b: A family pays ten thousand euros to free a kidnapped relative
note: Gift versus ransom: the same transfer under different rules.

a: A believer gives a tenth of her income to her church
b: A worker pays a tenth of her income as income tax
note: Tithe versus tax: same share, different norm set.

a: A referee holds up a red card to a player during a match
b: A stranger holds up a red card to a passer-by in the street
note: Counts as a dismissal only in context.

a: A woman listens to a podcast on economics while commuting by train
b: A woman commutes by train
note: Concurrent events: the podcast is a second event with its own partition.

a: A cook chops onions as one step in making a soup for dinner
b: A cook chops onions
note: Part-of: the chopping is a sub-event of the soup.

a: A man threatens a shopkeeper, who then hands over the till money
b: A shopkeeper hands over the till money
note: Causal chain: a prior threat event explains the second.

a: A woman walks to the station while phoning her mother
b: A woman walks to the station
note: Concurrency: a separate call event runs alongside the walk.

a: A man brushes his teeth before bed
b: Before bed, a man brushes his teeth
note: A paraphrase: every layer should agree, so A-identical is expected (a retest check).

a: A cashier scans a customer's groceries
b: At the till, a customer's groceries are scanned by the cashier
note: A paraphrase: every layer should agree, so A-identical is expected (a retest check).

a: A girl feeds her cat in the morning
b: In the morning a girl gives her cat its food
note: A paraphrase: every layer should agree, so A-identical is expected (a retest check).

a: A neighbour waters the plants of a person on holiday
b: While a person is on holiday, a neighbour waters their plants
note: A paraphrase: every layer should agree, so A-identical is expected (a retest check).

a: A student submits her thesis online
b: Online, a student hands in her thesis
note: A paraphrase: every layer should agree, so A-identical is expected (a retest check).

a: A baker bakes bread before dawn
b: Before dawn, a baker bakes the loaves
note: A paraphrase: every layer should agree, so A-identical is expected (a retest check).

a: A driver stops at a red light
b: A driver halts as the light turns red
note: A paraphrase: every layer should agree, so A-identical is expected (a retest check).

a: A father reads a bedtime story to his son
b: A son is read a bedtime story by his father
note: A paraphrase: every layer should agree, so A-identical is expected (a retest check).

a: A nurse takes a patient's blood pressure
b: A patient has her blood pressure taken by a nurse
note: A paraphrase: every layer should agree, so A-identical is expected (a retest check).

a: A farmer sells vegetables at the market
b: At the market, a farmer sells his vegetables
note: A paraphrase: every layer should agree, so A-identical is expected (a retest check).
